title: The King's Beast
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: In a kingdom resembling ancient China, the Ajin, people with animal features, are treated as second-class: men are conscripted, women pushed into brothels, and boys with powers made 'beast-servants' to royals (Viz blurb via AniList; ANN). Rangetsu, a fox Ajin, disguises herself as a man to serve Prince Tenyou, whom she blames for her twin brother Sogetsu's death, then learns he may not be the killer (ANN). Romance with Tenyou grows amid palace intrigue; complete in 18 volumes, set in the world of Dawn of the Arcana (MU).
life_message: Systemic oppression must be seen and resisted, and the truth matters more than revenge built on assumptions.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Rigid caste order of the palace shown as unjust.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Hierarchy present but critiqued as oppression (ANN 'systemic oppression').

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Imperial court traditions; no strong stance in sources.

folkways.japan: A Chinese-style imperial court seen through Japanese shoujo conventions, with cross-dressing and court intrigue as genre staples.

delivery.evidence: ANN reviewer notes the book is 'somewhat heavy-handed' while treating oppression as central to the plot (vol. 1 only).
delivery.note: Oppression is shown mainly through the system's effects; how its defenders are drawn is not established (to verify).

winners_losers: Sympathy lies with the Ajin and with Rangetsu; the oppressive court system is the antagonist, and Prince Tenyou turns out more complex than she assumed.
